_comment: THE COMMITTED DEFAULTS for the model router, same contract as
config/fleet.example.json: every value here is documentation-safe (RFC 5737
TEST-NET-3 addresses, generic host names), so the public tree never carries
real infrastructure and is publishable by construction rather than by a
scrub. A private config/model-router.json overrides it and is gitignored.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. It did not, and four readers wanted it:
scripts/csd-model-router, scripts/csd-lab-console (three call sites) and
scripts/csd-autodev-loop. Two of them fail soft -- `_read_json` returns {}
-- so on a fresh clone the console reported an empty cluster and ti_ok()
was unconditionally False, which is what failed eleven tests. The third
fails closed and says so. A config that only exists on one machine is not a
default, it is an undeclared dependency.
WHAT THIS FILE OWNS, AND WHAT LITELLM OWNS. Checked against LiteLLM's
router documentation rather than assumed. LiteLLM natively provides routing
strategies (simple-shuffle, latency-based, usage-based-v2, least-busy,
cost-based), deployment `order` and `weight`, `allowed_fails` and
`cooldown_time`, `num_retries`, `max_parallel_requests`, `rpm`/`tpm`,
health-check filtering, context-window pre-call checks, `model_group_alias`
and fallbacks. NONE of that belongs here and none of it is restated here.
LiteLLM has NO notion of GPU memory, model swapping on a device, or
physical hardware capability matching -- that is this file's whole subject:
whether a model can be resident on a given card right now, and what must be
evicted for it to be. `vram_mib`, `safeguard_mib`, `needs_caps`,
`exclusive_with`, `ttl_s`, `runtime` and the `pool` block have no LiteLLM
equivalent.
KNOWN DUPLICATION, recorded rather than silently carried. `aliases.*.jobs`
restates what LiteLLM's `model_group_alias` expresses, and
`aliases.*.host_pref` restates what `model_list[].litellm_params.api_base`
already encodes. Role-to-model is therefore stated in THREE places -- here,
config/roles.json, and the gateway -- which is a drift surface under the
one property the review gate depends on (reviewer and implementer resolving
to different weights). Deduplicating it changes this schema, so it is a
goal rather than an edit: the private file is canonical and its shape must
not fork from this one.
SECRETS ARE NOT HERE AND NEVER WILL BE. Addresses and capability labels
only; credentials are injected at run time from the agent's own vault.

host-a._comment: The swap-out card: whichever model is implementing holds it.

host-gpu-b._comment: Resident, and never the implementer's model -- it answers WHILE the implementer keeps its weights loaded. See docs/AGENT-ORGANISATION.md.

host-gpu-b-1080ti._comment: A VFIO guest on host-gpu-b, so it has its own address. `live` is asserted by nvidia-smi in the guest, never inferred: retrieval and indexing move here only when something has SEEN the card, because RAG on the reasoning cards is what this placement exists to avoid.

llama.cpp._comment: structured_output is the MECHANISM, not whether it works: llama-server converts a subset of JSON Schema to GBNF, and `response_format: json_schema` has documented breakage across versions where `json_object` behaves differently. G-CAPS-1 probes it rather than trusting this field.

bitnet-cpp._comment: NO IMAGE YET, and the probe reports it missing rather than assuming a default. Best-in-class for BitNet 1.58; do not force vLLM or llama.cpp onto a w1.58 model unless it has been measured. `structured_output: null` means UNKNOWN, not none -- it is a llama.cpp derivative so GBNF is plausible and unverified, which is exactly the distinction an absent image forces you to keep.

pool._comment: preempt_autodev: false is the policy deploy/systemd/fleet-gpu-mode-review.service encodes as `Restart=no`. A review container that restarts itself wins the race for the CDI device and the published port, which is preempting autodev once per crash. headroom_mib is reserved, not usable: `combined_mib` minus headroom is what a pooled model may actually claim.

local/embed._comment: Ordered preference, not a fallback chain the router invents: the 1080 Ti first so retrieval stays off the two reasoning cards, host-gpu-b only when the guest is not live.
